caseno: Criminal Appeal Nos. 192, 193 of 1994 and Government Appeal No. 25 of 1995.
lawyer:
Serajul Huq with Abdul Malek, Anisul Huq, ABM Golam Majid, Taufique Karim and M Imman Ali, Advocates — For the Appellants in Criminal Appeal No. 192 of 1994 
Khondker Mahbub Hossain with Golam Kibria, Md. Afzal Hossain, Harun-or-Rashid and Khurshida Bilkis Banu, Advocates — For the Appellant in Criminal Appeal No. 193 of 1994. 
AFM Shahid, Deputy Attorney-General, with Syed Abu Kowser, Assistant Attorney-General —For the Respondents in Criminal Appeal Nos. 192-93 of 1994 and for the Appellant in Govt. Appeal No. 25 of 1995. 
Yusuf Hossain Humayun, Advocate — For the Accused-Respondents in Govt. Appeal No. 25 of 1995.
parties:
Zahirul Alam Kamal and another ----- Appellant
Vs.
State Respondent (In CA No. 192 of 1994) Khondker Zillul Bari  ----- Appellant
Vs.
State Respondent (In CA No. 193 of 1994)
State ----- Appellant
Vs
Farida Jesmin & Ors ----- Respondents
(In Govt. Appeal No. 25 of 1995)
full_judgment:
Md. Mozammel Hoque J: Criminal Appeal No. 193 of 1994 has been filed by accused-appellant Khondker Zillul Bari and Criminal Appeal No. 192 of 1994 has been filed by accused-appellants Zahirul Alam Kamal and Nasiruddin Jamal. The Government also preferred an appeal being Government Appeal No. 25 of 1995 against the three accused who were acquitted by the trial Court. Since all the aforesaid three appeals have arisen out of the same judgment of conviction and sentence passed in Sessions Case No. 38 of 1990 by the learned Sessions Judge, Barisal, those were heard together and are being disposed of by one judgment.

2. The prosecution case, in short, is that one Faujia Rahman Chapa, the daughter of Sarder Matiur Rahman of Barisal Town, was married to one Shahidul Alam, second son of Mr. Khalilur Rahman who is the owner of Raphco Laboratories, Barisal, in the year 1984. This Faujia Rahman Chapa, hereinafter referred to as Chapa, was staying with her minor son Shakkhar aged about two years in the house of her father-in-law at Fakirbari Road of Barisal Town. At the relevant time the father-in-law and mother-in-law of the victim accompanied by three sons including the husband of Chapa went to Calcutta for treatment of her father-in-law who was suffering from heart trouble.

3. In the night following 18-10-89, besides deceased Chapa and her son Shakkhar, Nasiruddin Jamal and Zahirul Alam Kamal, two other sons of Khalilur Rahman, one daughter Jasminara anct her husband Khondker Zillul Bari and two daughters-in-law, namely, Farida Jesmin and Afroza Begum Bijli and other servants were staying in that house. In the morning of 19-10-89 at about 10-00/11-00 AM there was a row in front of the house of Mr. Khalilur Rahman that an accident took place in the house due to electric shock. At about 11-00 AM the Officer-in-Charge of the Kotwali Police Station received information over telephone to the effect that the daughter-in-law of Khalilur Rahman died in the house. The OC of Kotwali Police Station lodged a GD entry to that effect and being accompanied by some police officers he came to the house of Khalilur Rahman. When he reached the house of Khalilur Rahman he was informed by the inmates of the house that Chapa died. He was told that Chapa was taken to hospital. Then the OC went to the hospital and found some persons of the house of Khalilur Rahman. He asked them to lodge Ejahar. Then he saw the dead body of Chapa and thereafter he came back to the Thana leaving behind one police officer to prepare inquest report. He received an Ejahar in the police station at 1-00 PM through Mr. Ziaul Hoque Babul, an Advocate, which was written by another Advocate of the Barisal Bar, namely, Mr. Golam Abbas Chowdhury. That Ejahar was signed by Md. Nasiruddin Jamal. On the basis of that First Information Report the OC directed a Sub-Inspector of Police to hold investigation into the case.

4. It was the further case that at 10-30 AM this Nasiruddin informed the father of the deceased Chapa over telephone that Chapa had an accident. Then Mr. Rahman rushed to the house of Mr. Khalilur Rahman where Nasiruddin Jamal informed that Chapa was no longer alive. He then went to the room where Chapa was staying in the previous night. Looking in the room and the movement of the inmates of the house, he became suspicious about the death of Chapa. He also found that Shakkhar, the son of Chapa, was not in the house and on query he came to know that Shakkar was also injured. Thereafter, he left for hospital to see Chapa and on the way he also informed his wife about this occurrence. In the hospital the parents of Chapa wanted to see the dead body of Chapa, but Zahirul Alam Kamal and Zillul Bari did not allow them to see the dead body. They brought the dead body of Chapa in the hospital by the micro-bus of their Laboratory. The attending Doctor declared that the patient died 6/7 hours earlier. In the meantime, after receipt of the Ejahar from Nasiruddin Jamal inquest report was prepared by SI Nawsher Ali. Then the dead body was sent for post-mortem examination.

5. SI Mr. Sree Dam Devnath continued investigation of the case till 15-11-89. He examined some witnesses and recorded their statements under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. He also seized alamats, and statements of some of the witnesses were recorded by the Magistrate under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The case was then handed over to the CID on 16-11-89 and one Mr. Bimal Chandra Das, Inspector of CID, took over the charge of investigation. He also visited the place of occurrence, examined the witnesses and seized alamats and on the basis of the investigation it appeared to him that Ejahar lodged by Nasiruddin Jamal was not correct. He found that though Chapa was dead, the dead body was deliberately removed from the place of occurrence with a view to cause disappearance of the evidence. After preliminary investigation he submitted FRT in the case lodged by Nasiruddin Jamal and then he suo motu lodged the First Information Report against the six accused persons, namely, Zahirul Alam Kamal, Nasiruddin Jamal, Khondker Zillul Bari, Farida Jasmin, Jasminara and Afroza Begum Bijli. After investigating into the matter, the CID Inspector submitted charge-sheet against all the six accused under sections 302/307/201/34 of the Penal Code, Prosecution examined as many as 23 witnesses in the instant case and they were cross-examined by the defence. In the instant case the Sessions Judge framed charges against the six accused persons.

6. From the trend of cross-examination the defence case appeared to be that on the night of occurrence Chapa along with her son Shakkar was sleeping in a bed adjacent to a window and some miscreants, in order to take away her ornaments from her neck, killed her from outside the window. When Chapa did not rise from the bed in the morning, they saw through the window of the corridor that she was lying injured on her bed. Seeing this condition they broke open the door and took Chapa to the hospital for treatment. They are not liable for the murder of Chapa and they have been falsely implicated in the case at the instance of their business rivals. In the First Information Report submitted by Nasiruddin Jamal, he also stated that Chapa was killed by unknown assailants of outside.

7. Description of evidence of different witnesses may be given to the effect that in total 22 witnesses were examined by the prosecution. PWs 1 and 23 is one and same man, that is, the informant as well as the Investigating Officer of the instant case. PWs. 3 and 5 are parents of victim Chapa, PW 15 is brother of Chapa, PWs. 8, 12 and 18 are police officers who were attached at the relevant time with Kotwali Police Station. PW 11 is the doctor who held post-mortem examination. PWs. 19, 20 and 21 are three doctors who were attached at the relevant time in the Sher-e-Bangla Medical College Hospital. PWs. 4 and 9 are two nurses who were also attached with the same hospital at the relevant time. PW 6 is a constable who identified the dead body of Chapa before the doctor who held post-mortem examination. PWs, 10 and 14 are the two employees of Barisal Electric Supply Division. PW 2 is an Advocate of Barisal Bar. PW 7 is a Professor of Chemistry Department of Barisal BM College and PW 13 is a friend of victim Chapa and Mr. Shahidul Alam, husband of victim Chapa, was the Court witness. After examination of the aforesaid witnesses, considering the material evidence on record and hearing the arguments, the learned Sessions Judge, Barisal, found the accused Zahirul Alam Kamal, Nasiruddin Jamal and Khondker Zillul Bari guilty under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and also under sections 201/34 of the Penal Code and they were convicted and sentenced to suffer imprisonment for life and also to pay a fine of Taka 10,000.00 each, in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year more. They were also convicted under sections 201/34 of the Penal Code and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for three years and also to pay a fine of Taka 5,000.00 each, in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for six months more. Accused Farida Jasmin, Jasminara and Afroza Begum Bijli were acquitted from the charges levelled against them. Accused-appellants Zahirul Alam Kamal, Nasiruddin Jamal and Khondker Zillul Bari were acquitted from the charge under sections 307/34 of the Penal Code. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment of conviction and sentence accused-appellant Khondker Zillul Bari preferred this Criminal Appeal No. 193 of 1994 and other two accused-appellants preferred Criminal Appeal No. 192 of 1994. Government also preferred an appeal being Government Appeal No. 25 of 1995 against the order of acquittal of three female accused as stated above.

8. So, it appears that this accused-appellant Nasiruddin Jamal lodged an First Information Report on 19-10-89 with the Kotwali Police Station stating that some unknown assailants murdered his sister-in-law, that is, Chapa Bhabi, by using sharp cutting weapons. As we have stated earlier that after investigation an FRT was submitted in that case, because the police did not believe the story of Nasiruddin Jamal as made out in his First Information Report dated 19-10-89 and on the same day when FRT was submitted, the Investigating Officer himself as informant instituted the present criminal case against the present appellants and three others.

9. PW 1 is the CID Inspector Mr. Bimal Kumar Das who was the informant as well as the Investigating Officer in the case. He stated in detail the prosecution story as given in the First Information Report lodged by him. He visited the place of occurrence, examined the witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and seized several alamats from the house and being satisfied on the basis of the materials on record he submitted charge-sheet under sections 302/307/201/34 of the Penal Code against the accused. PW 2 is an Advocate who is living near the house of Khalilur Rahman. Re stated that hearing that some accident took place due to electricity trouble he gave a ring to telephone No. 3218 to the clectrice office and thereafter he went to the house of Khalilur Rahman and came to know that the dead body of Chapa was taken to hospital. He further stated that he did not hear anything about accident of electricity.

10. PW 3 is the father of deceased Chapa. He has given family description of the house of Khalilur Rahman. He stated that Farida Jasmin is the oldest daughter-in-law and Afroza Begum Bijli is the wife of Jamal. Jasminara is the daughter of Khalilur Rahman and her husband is Zillul Bari. He came to the house and heard from the inmates of the house that Chapa got an accident. He heard from Jamal that Chapa was no more. Then he went into the room of Chapa and then he went to the hospital. He also informed his wife that Chapa was taken to hospital. He had stated that he and his wife wanted to see the face of Chapa, but Kamal and Zillul Bari told them that they would not be able to tolerate the scene and in the hospital he heard that Chapa was taken here by the inmates of the house. He was cross-examined at length by the defence. He stated that he came to know from maid servants Fatima and Rawshanara secretly that in that night at about 10-00 PM there was a quarrel in between Chapa and Jesminara in the dining room on Chalita. Chapa took some Chalita prepared by Jasminara and Jasminara told Chapa that it was prepared for her husband, so why she took it. There was quarrel in between Chapa and Jasminara and at one stage Chapa stated that she loved her husband now very much, but before marriage where was that love and she would disclose everything what happened before marriage. In that night Chapa without taking her food went to her bed. PW 4 is the Senior Staff Nurse of Sher-e-Bangla Medical College Hospital and she described as to when Chapa was taken to hospital and what she did with Chapa as she was the nurse. Doctor told that Chapa died 6/7 hours back. PW 5 is the mother of Chapa. She stated that Chapa was her eldest daughter. She was a student of M.Sc. Class. Chapa was at the relevant time pregnant for 3/4 months and her son Shakkhar did not take breast milk. On 19-10-89 her husband told her that Chapa got an accident. She also went to the hospital to see Chapa. This witness stated that in that night there was a quarrel in between Jasminara and Chapa in the dining room over Chalita. Chapa took some piece of Chalita and Jasminara objected to it and told her as to why she had taken that Chalita, because she kept it for her husband. At that time Chapa told her that she had so much love for her husband; she would disclose everything what happened before marriage. She also made some description of the house and as to how she came there and what she came to know about this accident. She was cross-examined. She stated that maid servants Fatima and Rowshanara were staying in the ground floor and excepting this Chalita incident no other incident was disclosed to her by the maid servants.

11. PW 6 is the Sub-Inspector of Police of Kotwali Police Station. He held the inquest of the dead body and identified the dead body. PW 7 is the Head of the Department of Chemistry of BM College. He knew Faujia Rahman Chapa as she was the student of his Department. On the date of occurrence she had practical class, but she did not go to class on that day. On query he came to know that Chapa was dead. He further stated in cross-examination that Kamal was a student of his Department. He came to know at about 11-00 AM about the death of Chapa.

12. PW 8 is Sub-Inspector of Police of Kotwali Police Station. He was directed by the OC to go to Sher-e-Bangla Medical College Hospital on 19-10-89 to hold inquest on the dead body. He went there and the OC told him that a case has already been started and with reference to that case he is to hold the inquest. The dead body of Chapa was identified by her elder brother Amin Ahsan alias Palash. Inquest report was signed by eight witnesses. In the inquest report he stated that in the left side of her head there were marks of four cut injuries which were caused by sharp cutting weapons. Twelve injuries were on different parts of the face and head and no other injury was found at any portion of the dead body. PW 9 is another nurse of Sher-e-Bangla Medical College Hospital. She told that one Begmi took one boy aged about two and half years and his name was Shakkhar. This child was senseless and on the back side of his head she found some haematoma. Begmi told her that he got accident by current from a fan. Thereafter she came to know that the mother of the child was dead. PW 10 is one Md. Abdus Salam Talukder. He was the Senior Scale Assistant Director of Electricity Office of Barisal. He stated that some complaint was received as regards accident of electricity on 19-10-89. PW 11 is Doctor Abdul Barek, Assistant Professor, Sher-e-Bangla Medical College. He held the post-mortem examination on the dead body of Chapa which he described in his deposition as well as he proved the post-mortem report. He stated that in his opinion Chapa got injuries and death was caused due to shock and haemorrhage from the injuries as the same were found in the body of Chapa. He was cross-examined in detail. Further, he stated that he held the post-mortem examination after receipt of the inquest report and chalan.

13. PW 12 is Md. Ruhul Islam who was the Officer-in-Charge of the Kotwali Police Statiton. On 19-10-89 he received a telephone call that in the house of Khalilur Rahman at Fakirbari Road a house-wife died. But the person who gave telephonic information did not disclose his identity. Thereafter he came with his force to the house of Mr. Khalilur Rahman and from the house he came to know that Chap, the daughter-in-law of Khalilur Rahman died. One woman was crying saying Chapa Bhabi died. Thereafter he went to the hospital and directed them to lodge First Information Report in the police station. On 27-3-89 he received a written First Information Report from CID Inspector Bimal Kumar Das. A regular First Information Report was lodged and criminal case was started against the six accused persons. PW 13 is one Laiju Begum who was the friend and neighbour of Chapa. She first came to know that Chapa got an accident. She also went to hospital and wanted to see the face of Chapa, but two unknown persons told her that it was not possible to show the face. Ultimately she saw the face of Chapa with blood. PW 14 was a Line-man Assistant of Barisal Electricity Office. He along with one Aziz went to Fakirbari Road and found the electricity in order in the house of Khalilur Rahman. When he came to know that electricity was there in the house, he came back. PW 15 is the younger brother of Chapa. He also came to know from shop-keeper that an accident took place and his father went to the hospital. He also went to the hospital and came to know that Chapa was dead. From his evidence it appears that Fatima, Begmi, Rawshanara, Minara, Taslima are the maid servants of the house of Khalilur Rahman. Kabir Hossain Potka, Ishaque Ali and Sayeed Hossain are the male servants and cooks of that house.

14. PW 26 is one Md. Salahuddin who stated that Chapa was the daughter of his eldest brother-in-law. He came to know about the accident and went to the hospital and saw Chapa covered by a Chadar. He was witness of the inquest report. PW 17 stated that Chapa was his maternal cousin. He was also witness in the inquest report. PW 18 is Sreedham Devnath who investigated into the First Information Report lodged by Zahirul Alam Kamal and submitted final report in the case. Thereafter he became the informant and lodged the First Information Report against six accused persons in the instant case. In details he has given the description as regards the materials which he got during investigation. Further, he has given a vivid description of different places and areas of the house of Khalilur Rahman and also the room where Chapa was killed. The description as regards the room was given to the effect that the room was 10X12 cubits where Chapa was sleeping in that night. There was one door and five windows and the measurements of the windows are 58"X58". All the five windows were of grill fittings. He found all the grills and the glasses of the windows intact. The gap of the grill was 10"X4". There were two parts of screen with the windows and he found no blood with the screen of the window. He stated that there was wooden door in her house and found the inter lock broken. There was one Chhitkini which was curved at the end. The informant of the First Information Report stated to him that seeing the door closed from inside, they broke open the door and entered into the room.

15. He seized 19 articles as alamats from the room. He also seized one piece of old Khat. He also found on the border of the Khat a sign of crescent like fukni blow having 1/2" size. He found one piece of GI pipe the length of which was about 28" and hairs of head were found at the end of that GI pipe. One of the inmates of the house informed him that pipe was called Fukni. That Fukni was used for firing the cooker. No sign was found that Fukni was used for firing the cooker. That GI pipe was found on the Khat. The rear portion of the mosquito-net was found tied with the stand of the khat. The screens of the windows have two parts measuring 60"X60". The mosquito-net and the window curtain were found intact. The window screens were found hanged. He got two broken teeth on the khat. He also got one shabol whose length was 11/4 cubits. He also seized the broken steel inter-lock. The bed was open where he got the broken teeth and pipe on the khat. He also got one old brick on the carnish outside the window. That carnish was nine inches (9") wide. With the above articles he seized 19 items and he proved the seizure list. He seized several articles from the roof of the building including one white check lungi blood stained. He seized the keys of almirah and inter-lock and he was informed that the mother-in-law of Chapa gave those keys to her. In total 17 keys were there. He also seized some cheque-books of different banks. He further stated that considering all these aspects in the matter he came to a conclusion that the persons who were in the house in that night are responsible for killing Chapa.

16. He could not finish the investigation and on 16-11-89 he made over all the papers and documents to CID Inspector Bimal Kumar Das. The windows of the building of Khalilur Rahman had no sun-shade, but it had only carnish which is 9" wide. From the carnish upto the lower side of the window the distance was 34". On the query of the Court he stated that the carnish was as long as the length of building itself and it is not possible for any man to climb on the carnish without the help of ladder. Accused Kamal was on remand for three occasions and in total for eight days. On the query from the Court he stated that he did not see any sign of removing the Khat of Chapa from its original position. There was no carpet on the floor. Floor was a mosaic one.

17. PW 19 is Doctor AKM Rafiqul Islam. He stated about the injuries of the boy Shakkhar which he found on the head. PW 20 is doctor Liakat Ali Khan who was on duty on that date. He stated that SI Nawsher Ali held the inquest on the dead body in his presence. PW 21 is Doctor Md. Rafiqul Kabir. He stated that on 19-10-89 he was on duty from 8-00 AM upto 2 PM and at about 11-00 AM some persons brought one lady patient in the emergency ward. Being informed by the nurse, he went to see the patient and after examining her he declared the patient dead and she was brought dead. He examined the dead body and found injuries on the head and face of the deceased. He found the dead body hard and she died about 5/6 hours back. Thereafter, he came to know that the name of the lady was Faujia Rahman Chapa and she was brought there by her brother-in-law Kamal and 2/3 other persons. He was cross-examined by the defence. PW 22 was the Magistrate. He recorded the statements of Khondker Zillul Bari on 29-10-89 under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. He recorded the statements in the following way that after breaking the door this Zillul Bari went into the room and on removing the mosquito-net he found deceased Chapa blood stained on the bed lying her face down on the khat and found one 1-1/2 cubit length GI pipe. He also found black spot on the middle point of neck. He opined that somebody entered into the room of Chapa and killed her. He found Chapa within the mosquito-net lying with bleeding injuries.

18. PW 23 is the Inspector of CID who submitted charge-sheet in the instant case. He investigated into the case, took statements of the witnesses and he also took all the papers and documents which were seized by the previous Investigating Officer. Thereafter he filed charge-sheet against the accused-appellants and three others. He stated that though there is no eye-witness in the case, the circumstantial evidence are there. On the basis of the circumstantial evidence he filed the charge-sheet against the accused-appellants and others. He has also given some description of the pipe, namely, Fukni and the seized alamats. He denied several suggestions given by the defence. He stated that during investigation by him he went upto to the carnish of the building. He climbed on the carnish by a ladder. The carnish is above 16' (sixteen feet) from the ground. He took several photographs while he climbed and measured the carnish.

19. Mr. Shahidul Alam was examined as Court witness. This Shahidul Alam is the husband of deceased Chapa. On the date of occurrence he was at Calcutta with his parents and other two brothers. He stated that generally they went to bed at 12'00 night or 01-00 AM. The front side of the Khat was about 8" or 9" away from the window. At the relevant time his son Shakkhor was aged about one year nine months and he took breast milk as well as Cerelac. At the relevant time there was no Darwan or night-guard. Main door was closed by the servant of the house and other gates of other floors were closed by the inmates who are residing in those floors. He had good relationship with Chapa. His father did not keep cheque books with Chapa. No cheque-book was recovered from the almirah of his wife, Chapa. Thereafter the accused were examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and all of them pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. They did not give any defence witness in their favour in the instant case. These are sum total of the evidence of the witnesses. When we will discuss the points raised by the learned Advocates, we will further discuss the evidence of the witnesses wherever it is necessary.

20. In Criminal Appeal No. 193 of 1994, Mr. Khondker Mahbub Hossain, the learned Advocate, appeared for accused-appellant Khondker Zillul Bari, in Criminal Appeal No.192 of 1994. Mr. Abdul Malek, the learned Advocate, appeared for accused-appellant Nasiruddin Zamal and Mr. Serajul Huq, the learned Advocate, appeared for accused-appellant Zahirul Alam Kamal and in Government Appeal No. 25 of 1995, Mr. Yusuf Hossain Humayun, the learned Advocate, appeared for the respondents. Mr. AFM Shahid, the learned Deputy Attorney-General with Mr. Syed Abu Kowser, Assistant Attorney-General, appeared for the respondents in Criminal Appeal Nos. 192 and 193 of 1994 and for the appellant in Government Appeal No. 25 of 1995.

21. In the instant case some facts are admitted by both the prosecution as well as the defence. Chapa was murdered in the fateful night in her own room and there were no eye-witnesses in the instant case. So, it is admitted position that in the night following 18.10.89 Chapa was murdered in her own room. But there was no eye-witness and, as such, the entire case depended on the circumstantial evidence. Now we are to examine as to how far the prosecution has been able to prove the case beyond all reasonable doubt against the appellants on the basis of the circumstantial evidence. The learned Advocate appearing for the appellants submitted that the present case is a case of no evidence and there was total misconception of the fact which led to an erroneous decision in the case. Since there was no eye-witness in the case and since the entire case depends on the circumstantial evidence, motive must be ascertained first, but there was no motive to kill Chapa. The conviction and sentence is not sustainable in the eye of law. In this connection the learned Advocates for the appellants have drawn our attention to the finding of the learned Sessions Judge where he has categorically found that no motive could be proved in the instant case by the prosecution.

<u>22. The learned Deputy Attorney-General, on the other hand, submitted that circumstances as considered by the learned Sessions Judge are reasonable and believeable. He submitted that the story of causing injuries on the face and head of the victim through the window is absolutely an absurdity and standing on the 9" wide carnish such injuries on the face and head could not be inflicted from outside by the alleged fukni by any outsider. Several circumstances pointed out the guilt of the accused. He further submits that the conducts of the accused are destructive to the presumption of innocence. Failure on the part of the accused to give proper and reasonable explanation about the cause of murder will lead to a conclusion that in fact they committed this murder. Motive is to be gathered from the facts and circumstances of the case. Particularly, the dispute over Chalita as well as the fact that father-in-law of Chapa put trust on her instead of other sons and daughters and daughter-in-law of the house could not be ignored altogether. In a criminal case it is the duty of the prosecution to prove the guilt of the accused. But in certain cases and under certain circumstances the accused are also liable to give an explanation as to the cause of the occurrence. It is on evidence that other gates of the house of Khalilur Rahman were closed and it was not possible and there was no evidence also to show that some miscreants came from outside of the house, entered into the house through the doors and thereafter went upto the first floor of the building and went into the room of Chapa and killed her. From the defence case itself it appears that excepting the window where the khat of deceased Chapa was lying in no other way this occurrence could be done by any person from outside. So, Chapa was killed in her own room and other outsider could not enter into the room. The strong explanation of the accused who were the inmates of the house was that Chapa was killed by the outside miscreants standing on the 9" wide carnish and through the window with the help of a Fukni, that is, one and half cubit long G I pipe.</u>

23. Since they have given an explanation, let us see as to whether this is at all believeable or not, or whether they have been able to prove it. In this connection if we analyse the evidence of PW 18, we get the vivid description of the position of the room as well as the window through which allegedly the outsider committed this murder in order to take the ornaments of Chapa. It was alleged that standing on the carnish, the outsider committed this offence. But the carnish is only 9" (nine inches) wide and on the carnish one brick was found which means standing on the carnish it was not possible to do anything through the window and that is why the alleged murderer took brick on the carnish. Evidence was that without the ladder it was not possible to climb upon the carnish. But it is not humanly possible to do anything or any criminal offence like the present one standing on 9" wide carnish of the building. Further, it was proved that there was no blood stained mark with the screen of the window, and the mosquito-net remained intact and dead body was found under the mosquito-net by the inmates of the house. This untorn mosquito-net actually speaks volumes about the alleged story as given by the accused of the case. It further appears that there was no blood stained mark with mosquito-net and the screen of the window. Only it shows that some blood stained mark was found with one grill of the window. All the injuries were inflicted on the face and head of Chapa and two teath were broken. It is submitted from the State that standing on nine inches wide carnish a man can never inflict or cause injuries on the head and face of Chapa in the fashion as they described. The small boy also got injury on his head. The inmates further stated that when Chapa did not rise at 9-10 AM, they peeped through the door and found Chapa lying on the bed with injuries and blood and there-after they broke open the door. PW 18 has given a picture of the entire room along with articles and the window through which the alleged murder was committed. The Investigating Officer also climbed on the nine inches wide carnish with the help of ladder and stated before the Court that it was not possible for any human being to cause any injury to the inmate of the room standing on such carnish. Further, the gap in the grill was 10"X 4" and through this gap it is impossible for a miscreant to cause death to an inmate who was lying on the khat inside the room.

<u>24. Considering the position of the building, the windows, the carnish as well as considering the facts that the window's screen as well as mosquito-net were not torn in any manner whatsoever and also considering the fact that no other persons from outside coming through the main gate or in any other manner could enter into the room of Chapa, we are of the view that it is impossible to cause several injuries on the face and head of Chapa through the window as per explanation given by the accused persons in the instant case. It further appears that the main gate was closed, while the collapsible gates of each floor were also closed by the inmates of that floor and there is no iota of evidence either direct or indirect that it was possible for some other persons to come inside the room from outside and cause such injuries on the face and head of the deceased. The learned Deputy Attorney-General further submits that all the injuries were caused on the face and head and two teeth of Chapa were broken. Standing on the carnish and through the grill of the window of one side such injuries could not be caused and these injuries were caused just from the front side of the deceased and not from outside of the room. This argument has got much force in the instant case in view of the fact that all injuries were caused on the face and head of the deceased. It is further suggested that if through the window some miscreants give any blow by the Fukni, then and there she would wake up, cry and call all the other inmates. To answer to this question learned Advocate for the appellants submits, it was possible that after giving one blow on the head she lost her sense and could not raise any hue and cry. But the thing remains that on the assessment of the evidence on record as well as from the findings of the learned Sessions Judge it appears to us that it was not possible for any outside miscreant to cause such injuries standing on nine inches wide carnish on the face and head of Chapa and kill her. In our view, the explanation given by the defence totally falls through and it is established that Chapa was killed in her room by the miscreants who living within the house went into her room caused injuries in such manner and ultimately she succumbed to the injuries.</u>

25. Facts and circumstances as shown in the instant case are not very much disputed, that means, Chapa was killed in her own room. But this is to be decided here as to who is or who are the assailant or assailants of Chapa. Since she was sleeping in her own room in the first floor of the building and since other inmates were there in that house in that fateful night, they have to give an explanation. In the First Information Report accused Jamal stated that some miscreants killed her and thereafter when the instant case was started against the present accused-appellants and others they took a plea and gave explanation that she , was murdered by outside-miscreants through the window for stealing her ornaments. Since the learned Sessions Judge has discussed in detail the evidence on record, we need not go to repeat the discussion and we will consider those portions of the evidence which are very much material for this case.

26. The learned Deputy Attorney-General submits that there was a motive to kill her, although Mr. Serajul Huq and Mr. Malek submit that no motive could be proved. As regards motive to kill Chapa the learned Deputy Attorney-General has drawn our attention to the evidence of PWs. 3 and 5, that is, father and mother of the deceased Chapa. They stated that some quarrel arose over taking Chalita and Chapa used some filthy language against the character of Jasminara, the daughter of Khalilur Rahman. On such filthy remarks the accused became angry and they hatched up a conspiracy to kill Chapa. But it appears in the eye of law this allegation or statement cannot be taken as evidence in view of the fact that both PWs. 3 and 5 stated that they heard it from the two maid servants of the house, but those two maid servante were not examined. So, this is merely hearsay evidence. Secondly, it was found that on the quarrel over Chalita the prosecution failed to prove any conspiracy to kill Chapa on such ground. Further, it appears to us that for such a trifling matter how inmates of the house including the hilsband of Jasminara would hatch up a conspiracy and kill Chapa in her own room. Further, it is alleged that all the inmates of the house were envious against Chapa in view of the fact that her father-in-law Khalilur Rahman relied on her and kept with her all the cheque-books of his business and even when they went to Calcutta, the mother-in-law of Chapa gave her all the keys of the house. The cheque-books were not seized from the room of Chapa, but some keys were found in her room. Merely because the keys of the house were given to Chapa by the mother-in-law, it could not be imagined that this fact alone will lead the accused to kill her and to that effect the prosecution failed to bring any evidence as to the hatching up a conspiracy to kill Chapa.

27. Mr. Serajul Huq submits that in a case of circumstantial evidence, motive must be proved and in support of his contention he has referred to the case of State vs. Lalu Miah, 39 DLR (AD) 177. From the Judgment of the trial Court it appears that even the learned Sessions Judge failed to point out any motive of murder. In a case like this motive of murder could have been gathered if the other inmates of the house, i. e. the servants, maid-servants and cooks were examined. Non-examination of those inmates of the house is a serious omission and laches on the part of the prosecution. But such a proposition of Mr. Huq cannot be universally accepted. It varies from the facts and circumstances of each individual case.

28. Let us see the case of accused-appellant Zillul Bari who was not a member of the family. He is the son-in-law (Jamai) of that house being husband of Jasminara and the prosecution story as well as the evidence could not prove any guilt against this Zillul Bari in view of the fact that he being a Jamai of the house was in the fateful night staying with his wife there and when such an occurrence took place, it is quite natural for a relation that he should take steps for taking her to the hospital or to call doctor and give treatment. As a relation he only performed his moral obligation when such occurrence took place in the house. So, against Zillul Bari no case has been made out by the prosecution.

<u>29. Now, as to accused-appellants Jamal and Kamal and three other lady inmates of the house we are to see as to how far they were involved in the case. In that fateful night Chapa along with her minor son was sleeping in one room, in another Jamal with his wife was sleeping and in another room Kamal was staying. All the rooms were in the first floor of the building. So, in that night the six accused persons were staying in the first floor and in the ground floor the eight servants, maid-servants and cooks were staying. They are Fatima, Begmi, Rawshanara, Kinara and Taslima. They all are maid servants. Then Kabir Hossain Potka, Ishaque All Fakir and Sayed Hossain they all are cooks and other servants of that house. So, in total 14 persons, excepting Chapa and her child, were staying in the house on that fateful night. Since the accused failed to establish the explanation as to the cause of death of Chapa and since from the materials on record it appears that it was not possible for any other outsider-miscreants to enter into the house and the room of Chapa and commit this offence, the natural conclusion unmistakably goes to show that Chapa was killed not by any outsider, but by the inmate or inmates of the house. Now, the question is actually who is or who of those inmates of the house of Khalilur Rahman were liable to commit this offence of murder of Chapa. In a criminal case it is individual liability of each and every accused and guilt of each and every accused must be proved beyond all reasonable doubt. Since there were 14 inmates in the house in that fateful night, now the prosecution must prove beyond all reasonable doubt that such and such inmate or inmates of the house or one or two or more inmates jointly or separately committed this offence of murder. It might be done by one man or two or more severally or collectively, but evidence must come either direct or circumstantial to that effect. It cannot be said that six accused or all the 14 inmates of the house in that fateful night are jointly liable for the murder. This proposition will be absolutely preposterous one in view of the fact that the prosecution has failed to prove any motive to commit such a heinous offence in the house. Further, the prosecution has failed to adduce any evidence to show that the victim Chapa had any ill feeling or enmity or bad relationship with any of the inmates of the house. But the thing remains that she was murdered by the inmates of the house. Out of 14 persons, such an offence might be committed by one person or two persons or more. It might be that one inmate and one servant committed this murder. It might be that one inmate with two male servants or maid-servants committed the offence. It might be that two of the inmates of the first floor and 2/3 inmates of the ground floor conjointly committed this offence. Since there is no eye-witness, liability to commit murder must be fixed against the accused without any sort of doubt. So, we are to fix or to ascertain as to actually out of 14 inmates who is or who are liable for committing this offence of murder of Chapa.</u>

<u>30. We have gone through the lengthy judgment of the learned Sessions Judge who took much pains in order to find out the actual offender on the basis of only circumstantial evidence and subsequent conduct of the three appellants. We fully appreciate the long discussion on circumstantial evidence as made by the learned Sessions Judge in his judgment. We also accept the views of the learned Sessions Judge that murder was committed not by the outsider-miscreants, but by the inmates of the house. We cannot but point out one thing of the judgment i.e. the learned Sessions Judge himself was in doubt as to who actually caused the murder and that is why he expressed his views, "It is true that there is no sufficient evidence as to what actually happened in that night in the house of the accused. But from the conduct of accused Kamal, Jamal and Zillul Bari it is clear that from the very beginning they acted in such a manner as to cause disappearance of the evidence and to hide the real fact. "We find that actually on the apprehension that as they tried to cause disappearance of evidence and hide the facts, the learned Sessions Judge found them guilty solely relying upon their subsequent conduct. It is difficult for us to accept such finding as to guilt under sections 302/201/34 of the Penal Code as because the conclusion of the findings of the learned Sessions Judge was just based on the subsequent conduct of the accused. Subsequent conduct may be considered along with other evidence, but it cannot be accepted as ground for awarding conviction under sections 302/201/34 of the Penal Code.</u>

<u>31. We have heard the learned Advocate, of both sides and perused the materials on record as well as the findings of the learned Sessions Judge as given in his judgment. The learned Sessions Judge on the basis of the circumstantial evidence as discussed in his judgment believed that three persons, namely, Jamal, Kamal and Zillul Bari, committed this offence and he acquitted the three lady inmates of the house. But it appears to us that the prosecution has totally failed even by circumstantial evidence to fix the person, that is, who is or who are actually responsible for killing Chapa in the above manner. If any doubt arises in the mind of a Judge, it is difficult to give conviction to a person and it is the established principle that an accused must always be given the benefit of doubt in any case however heinous it might be if the prosecution fails to prove the case beyond all reasonable doubt against him. It is the established principle that one guilty person may be acquitted on benefit of doubt, but an innocent person must not be punished. So, considering the material evidence on record we are required to fix as to who is or who are the actual culprits who committed this offence of murder of Chapa. In our view, this is a case of extreme benefit of doubt and, as such, the accused-appellants are entitled to such benefit in the instant case. Since, either by the direct evidence or by indirect evidence or by any other circumstantial evidence the prosecution has failed to fix liability for causing murder to a particular person or persons of that house it is difficult for us to maintain the conviction and sentence awarded against the three accused-appellants in these two appeals and, as such, they are entitled to acquittal on the ground of benefit of doubt.</u>

32. The Government has also preferred Government Appeal No. 25 of 1995. That appeal was preferred against three ladies accused who were acquitted by the learned Sessions Judge. So, we think that no further or separate discussion is required to consider the appeal of the Government with regard to the three lady respondents. Our discussions and findings made above will also cover this appeal and, as such, no separate finding is necessary.

33. In the result, both the appeals, namely, Criminal Appeal No. 193 of 1994 and Criminal Appeal No. 192 of 1994, are allowed and the judgment of conviction and sentence passed against the three accused-appellants is hereby set aside. Accused-appellants Khondker Zillul Bari and Nasiruddin Jamal, who are on bail, are discharged from their bail bonds and let accused-appellant Zahirul Alam Kamal be released forthwith if not wanted in connection with any other case. Let an advance order of release be issued.

34. The appeal, namely, Government, Appeal No. 25 of 1995 is hereby dismissed.

35. Before parting with this case we express our deep sorrow for the innocent departed soul of the young girl student Chapa who became victim of such a heinous crime. It is not possible for us to detect or find out the actual offender of killing of Chapa on the basis of the earthly evidence as available on record and punish him under earthly law, but we pray to Almighty Allah that the real and actual murderer or murderers of Chapa must be punished by Him as He being Alimul-gaib saw everything regarding the murder of Chapa.

36. Send down the LC records immediately to the trial Court concerned.

End.
